query: Explain why some Qatar Airways Business-Class flights receive a non-recommended (Recommended = no) result.

per_column.name: Review_Length
per_column.rationale: Raw text length is a generic surface feature with little analytical leverage for explaining non-recommendation. It is trivially derivable from the review text, though the specific counts don't obviously match word/char counts of the shown samples.

per_column.name: Rating_Variance
per_column.rationale: Variance across the sub-ratings is a genuine new axis (inconsistent experiences may drive non-recommendation), derivable from the numeric rating columns. Some values are hard to verify but the quantity is plausibly computed from present fields.

per_column.name: Complaint_Count
per_column.rationale: Counting distinct complaints in the text is highly relevant to explaining non-recommendation. Extraction is a warranted reading, though some samples look questionable (the seat-recline row with clear grievances scored 0), indicating imperfect grounding.

per_column.name: Low_Rating_Count
per_column.rationale: Number of low sub-ratings directly relates to why a flight is not recommended and is derivable from the rating columns. The seat-recline sample scoring 5 low ratings seems inconsistent with a mostly-praised check-in narrative, but numeric fields aren't shown to fully verify.

per_column.name: Has_Major_Complaint
per_column.rationale: A flag for a serious complaint (e.g., lost bag, refused reimbursement) gives a useful categorical axis and is a warranted reading of the text, as seen in the JFK-bag sample scoring 1.

per_column.name: Overall_Low
per_column.rationale: A low-overall-rating flag is useful but partly redundant with the existing Overall Rating and closely correlated with Recommended. It is soundly derivable from the overall rating field.

per_column.name: Service_Comfort_Gap
per_column.rationale: The gap between service and comfort ratings is a genuine analytical axis that can explain dissatisfaction, derivable from the two rating columns. Some sample values are hard to fully verify but plausible.

judge.rationale: Most added columns (Complaint_Count, Low_Rating_Count, Has_Major_Complaint, Service_Comfort_Gap, Rating_Variance) provide genuine axes for explaining non-recommendation and are largely derivable from the review text and existing rating fields. Review_Length is a generic surface feature adding little leverage, and Overall_Low is somewhat redundant with existing columns. Groundedness is generally sound, but a few sample values (e.g., the seat-recline row scoring 0 complaints yet 5 low ratings) appear inconsistent with the source text, lowering confidence somewhat.
